Short answer: Consider an adjustable LED task lamp such as the Meadowlight Lamp from your catalog — it’s the best candidate in your saved lighting products for an energy-efficient office upgrade. 

Why I recommend it (and LED task lamps in general)
- LEDs use far less power than incandescent/halogen for the same light output (high lumens per watt), so an LED desk lamp typically reduces energy use and heat.
- Adjustable/task-style fixtures let you aim light where you need it, so you can use lower overall illuminance and still get good visual performance.
- Modern LED task lamps are often dimmable and offer selectable color temperatures (cooler 4000–5000 K for focused office work), which improves comfort and efficiency.

What my memory shows
- Your saved catalog includes an item called “Meadowlight Lamp” and other entries labeled “adjustable desk lamps,” “task lamps,” and “lighting products.” That indicates the Meadowlight is available in your inventory/catalog, but there are no technical specs in memory.

Claims that need verification (I can check these for you)
- Actual power draw (watts) and measured lumen output — needed to compute lumens-per-watt (efficacy).
- Whether the Meadowlight (or any candidate) is LED vs. another lamp type.
- Certification: Energy Star or DLC listing (confirms verified efficiency).
- Color temperature options and CRI (color rendering index) — CRI ≥ 80–90 is desirable for office work.
- Dimming type (smooth, flicker-free; triac vs. 0–10 V vs. PWM), dimming range, and whether dimmer is built-in or requires compatible control.
- Physical adjustability (arm reach, swivel, clamp or base) to fit your desk layout.
- Warranty and rated lifetime (hours) for the LEDs.
- Price/availability.

Checklist to pick the best energy-efficient desk lamp
- LED light source with manufacturer lumen and wattage specs (calculate lm/W).
- Energy Star or DLC certification if possible.
- CRI ≥ 80 (ideally ≥ 90) and a neutral-to-cool color temperature option (~4000 K).
- Dimmable with flicker-free driver.
- Adjustable arm/head and focused task lighting (not just ambient).
- Reasonable warranty (2+ years) and long rated life (20,000+ hours).

If you want, I can:
- Pull detailed specs for the Meadowlight Lamp and other catalog lamps and compare their lm/W, CRI, color temps, dimming, and certifications.
- Recommend one or two specific models (with verification) tailored to your desk size, budget, and preferred color temperature.

Which would you prefer: I’ll fetch Meadowlight’s full specs from your catalog now, or would you like a short list of criteria and external model suggestions?
